rootText: Home Lifestage Young Family Young Family Stability is especially key when you have young children to care for. Building a good foundation for protection and wealth will help give you peace of mind when it comes to your future and theirs. Contact us Prime a better future for your growing family Prioritise securing a safer and better tomorrow for you and your loved ones. High priority Protection In the event of unexpected circumstances such as critical illnesses, accidents or death, at least one or more dependants may be impacted. Your priority for protection: Health insurance for hospitalisation.Protection against accidents and major illnesses so that your needs during recovery continue to be met.Financial payout for death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability.Maternity insurance if you’re growing your family. Plan your protection High priority Wealth You are likely to have taken on more financial demands such as a home mortgage, your children’s education, and retirement. Your priority for wealth: Savings for immediate and future expenses.Retirement planning. Build your wealth Medium priority For Your Dependants Protecting your loved ones from the unexpected can allow you to focus on your responsibilities without constant worry. Your priority for your dependants: Health insurance for hospitalisation.Protection against accidents, death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability.Care plan for your parents. Protect your dependants Learn more about your needs Protection Wealth For your dependants Protection Safeguarding your health grows in importance as you embark on a new phase of life. Saving for your upcoming milestones will be easier when you don’t have to worry about medical expenses. What you already have¹ If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes: MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement. MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs. CareShield Life Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability What you may consider² With big-ticket items lined up in your future, being sufficiently protected is critical in ensuring that your savings can be used as intended – for the new life you’re building. National schemes do not fully cover: Hospitalisation An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) provides additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals. Critical Illness You’ll need coverage of 4x annual income. (Recommended)³ Death & Total and Permanent Disability You’ll need coverage of 9 – 10x annual income. (Recommended)³ Savings² To stay covered and accumulate savings over the years. Maternity Coverage for baby and mum. It’s recommended to spend at most 15% of take-home pay on insurance protection. Why act now Health crises can cause income loss and depletion of family funds². Ensure either partner can sustain the family if the other faces an unfortunate event. Connect with a Financial Representative for personalised coverage. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. Having a plan to grow your money steadily will help achieve your goals including future expenses and retiring comfortably with your partner. Basics – what you should have³ Emergency Funds At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses (including dependants) for rainy days. Legacy Planning A plan for a will, family trusts, life insurance, powers of attorney, and CPF nominations. Investment It is recommended to allocate at least 10%3 of your take-home pay for key milestones.
